record.title: Bannai et al.'s classification conjecture for spherical 3-distance 5-designs
record.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ be a spherical 3-distance 5-design.

**Bannai et al.'s classification conjecture.** One of the following holds: (1) $n=2$ and $C$ is a regular hexagon or a regular heptagon; (2) $C$ is a tight spherical 5-design; or (3) $C$ is derived from a tight spherical 7-design.

This conjecture asks for the classification of spherical 3-distance 5-designs. The paper rules out certain cases and reports verification in all dimensions $n\leq 1000$, but does not establish the classification in general.
record.source_name: Peter Boyvalenkov and Navid Safaei, “On 3-distance spherical 5-designs”, arXiv:2007.01895 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.01895

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2020).

record.title: Fractional Kowalik–Luzar–Škrekovski conjecture for high-girth planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph of girth at least five, and let $\fva(G)$ denote its fractional vertex-arboricity. **Fractional Kowalik–Lu\v{z}ar–Škrekovski conjecture.** Every planar graph of girth at least five has fractional vertex-arboricity at most $10/7$, that is, 
$$
\fva(G)\leq \frac{10}{7}.
$$
 This is the fractional analogue of the conjecture that such a graph has an induced forest on at least seven-tenths of its vertices. The paper records a best known induced-forest bound of $2n/3$ for planar graphs of girth at least five and leaves the proposed fractional bound open.
record.source_name: Marthe Bonamy, František Kardoš, Tom Kelly and Luke Postle, “Fractional vertex-arboricity of planar graphs”, arXiv:2009.12189 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.12189

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2020). “We initiate a systematic study of the fractional vertex-arboricity of planar graphs and demonstrate connections to open problems concerning both fractional coloring and the size of the largest induced forest in planar graphs.”

record.title: Infinite-family conjecture for self-similar congruences of the 19-regular partition function
record.statement:
Let $b_{19}(n)$ be the number of $19$-regular partitions of $n$. For a prime $p>3$, define $\alpha$ and $\beta$ by

$$
\alpha\equiv -3\cdot 8^{-1}\pmod p,\qquad 0<\alpha<p,
$$

$$
\beta=\left\lfloor\frac{3p}{8}\right\rfloor.
$$

**Infinite-family conjecture for $b_{19}$.** For a positive proportion of primes $p$, one has

$$
\sum_{n=0}^\infty b_{19}(2pn+2\alpha)q^n\equiv q^\beta\sum_{n=0}^\infty b_{19}(2n)q^{pn}
$$

modulo $2$.

This predicts that the displayed congruence for $p=5$ is the first member of an infinite family and would, by iteration, produce infinite families of even progressions. The source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: William J. Keith and Fabrizio Zanello, “Parity of the coefficients of certain eta-quotients”, arXiv:2010.09881 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.09881

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2020). “In the final section, we offer some concluding remarks, including applications to other classes of eta-quotients, and present further open questions that might be of interest for future investigations.”

record.title: Dekking's conjecture on the subword complexity of the Fibonacci-Thue-Morse sequence
record.statement:
Let $({\bf ftm}[n])_{n\geq 0}$ be the Fibonacci-Thue-Morse sequence, obtained by summing modulo $2$ the bits in the Fibonacci representation of $n$. Let $\rho_{\bf ftm}(n)$ denote its subword complexity, and define

$$
d(n):=\rho_{\bf ftm}(n+1)-\rho_{\bf ftm}(n).
$$

For each $i\geq 2$, let $F_i$ denote the $i$th Fibonacci number. **Dekking's conjecture.** The first-difference sequence of the subword complexity is

$$
(d(n))_{n\geq 0}=(1,2,4,6,10)\prod_{i\geq 2}6^{F_i+(-1)^i}\,8^{F_i},
$$

that is, it begins

$$
1,2,4,6,10,6,6,8,6,8,8,6,6,6,6,8,8,8,6,6,6,\ldots.
$$

The quantity $d(n)$ counts the right-special factors of length $n$ in the Fibonacci-Thue-Morse sequence. The paper proves this conjecture, so the asserted formula is no longer open.
record.source_name: Jeffrey Shallit, “Subword complexity of the Fibonacci-Thue-Morse sequence: the proof of Dekking's conjecture”, arXiv:2010.10956 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.10956

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of October 2020); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Minimal-volume conjecture for fullerenes with 10k atoms
record.statement:
Let $C_N$ be the class of fullerene isomers with $N$ atoms, and let $N=10k$ with $k\geq 2$. A nanotubical fullerene has a tubular part and two caps; a cap of type (a) is one of the four cap types considered in the paper. Let $D$ be a right-angled hyperbolic dodecahedron. **Minimal-volume conjecture for fullerenes with 10k atoms.** If a fullerene with $N=10k$ atoms, $k\geq 2$, has the minimal hyperbolic volume in the class $C_N$, then it is a nanotubical fullerene with caps of type (a), and its volume is given by

$$
\operatorname{vol}(F)=\left(\frac{N}{10}-1\right)\cdot\operatorname{vol}(D).
$$

The preceding proposition proves this volume formula for nanotubical fullerenes with caps of type (a), but does not prove that these fullerenes minimize volume in all of $C_N$.
record.source_name: Andrey Egorov and Andrei Vesnin, “On correlation of hyperbolic volumes of fullerenes with their properties”, arXiv:2011.02711 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.02711

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2020).

record.title: Borie's bijection conjecture for 1234-avoiding up-down permutations
record.statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer. An **up-down permutation of size $2n$** is a permutation of $\{1,\ldots,2n\}$ whose successive entries alternately rise and fall, and a permutation **avoids $1234$** if it has no increasing subsequence of length four. Let a **weighted Dyck path** be a Dyck path together with the weights described in Borie's construction; denote the relevant class by $WD_{2n}$. **Borie's conjecture.** There exists a combinatorial bijection between up-down permutations of size $2n$ avoiding $1234$ and a certain class of weighted Dyck paths. This conjecture proposes a new correspondence between two families counted by the three-dimensional Catalan numbers. The paper presents a more structured bijection resolving this existence claim, so the original conjecture is solved.
record.source_name: Justine Falque, “A Bijection Between Weighted Dyck Paths and 1234-avoiding Up-Down Permutations”, arXiv:2012.00122 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.00122

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of December 2020); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Extremal Ky Fan norms of the LI-matrix for trees
record.statement:
Let $T_n$ be a tree with $n\geq 12$ vertices. The path $P_n$, the tree $T_n$, and the star $K_{1,n-1}$ are compared using the Ky Fan $k$-norm of their LI-matrices, denoted by $||LI(\mathord{\cdot})||_{F_k}$.

**Tree extremal conjecture.**

$$
||LI(P_n)||_{F_k}\leq ||LI(T_n)||_{F_k}\leq ||LI(K_{1,n-1})||_{F_k}.
$$

Equality on the left holds if and only if $T_n\cong P_n$, and equality on the right holds if and only if $T_n\cong K_{1,n-1}$.

The claim proposes that the path and star uniquely minimize and maximize the relevant Ky Fan norm among trees on $n\geq 12$ vertices. The supplied text does not indicate whether this conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Zhen Lin, Lianying Miao, Guanglong Yu and Han Sheng, “On the Ky Fan k-norm of the LI-matrix of graphs”, arXiv:2012.11162 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.11162

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

record.title: Inclusion-exclusion positivity conjecture for Schubert polynomial specializations
record.statement:
Let $w\in S_n$ and let $u$ be a subword of $w$. For words $u\leq v\leq w$, write $\lvert w\rvert$ for word length, and let $\mathfrak{S}_{\operatorname{perm}(v)}({\bf 1})$ denote the principal specialization of the Schubert polynomial indexed by the permutation obtained from $v$. **Inclusion-exclusion positivity conjecture.**

$$
\sum_{u\leq v\leq w}(-1)^{\lvert w\rvert-\lvert v\rvert}\mathfrak{S}_{\operatorname{perm}(v)}({\bf 1})\geq 0.
$$

The result is proved in the paper for $1432$- and $1423$-avoiding permutations, and the conjecture extends that theorem to all permutations.
record.source_name: Karola Mészáros and Arthur Tanjaya, “Inclusion-exclusion on Schubert polynomials”, arXiv:2102.11179 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.11179

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2021).

record.title: Non-IR conjecture for paths and cycles
record.statement:
Let $P_n$ denote the path on $n$ vertices and $C_n$ the cycle on $n$ vertices. An **IR-graph** is a graph arising as an irredundance graph.

**Non-IR conjecture for paths and cycles.** The path $P_n$ is not an IR-graph for each $n\geq 3$, and the cycle $C_n$ is not an IR-graph for each $n\geq 5$.

These are open problems concerning which graphs can occur as irredundance graphs. They are stated together in the paper's list of conjectures and open problems and are attributed there to Mynhardt (2019).
record.source_name: C. M. Mynhardt and A. Roux, “Irredundance Trees of Diameter 3”, arXiv:2104.09004 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.09004

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2021).

record.title: Rota's unimodal conjecture for subspace numbers
record.statement:
Let $E=\{v_1,\ldots,v_n\}$ be a spanning subset of a $d$-dimensional complex vector space $V$, and let $w_i(E)$ denote the number of $i$-dimensional subspaces spanned by subsets of $E$. **Rota's unimodal conjecture.** There exists an index $j$ such that

$$
w_0(E)\leq\cdots\leq w_{j-1}(E)\leq w_j(E)\geq w_{j+1}(E)\geq\cdots\geq w_d(E).
$$

Rota proposed this conjecture in 1971 as another assertion concerning the numbers of subspaces spanned by subsets of $E$. The source provides no resolution or further status information, and the conjecture is part of the broader study of matroidal and combinatorial analogues of the Kähler package.
record.source_name: Laurenţiu G. Maxim and Jörg Schürmann, “Constructible sheaf complexes in complex geometry and Applications”, arXiv:2105.13069 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.13069

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2021).

record.title: The $q$-analog of the Markoff injectivity conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mu_q$ be the $q$-analog of the monoid homomorphism used to define $q$-Markoff numbers, and let $\mu_q(w)_{12}\in\mathbb{Z}[q]$ denote the corresponding entry above the diagonal. Let $\\{\mathtt{0},\mathtt{1}\\}^*$ be the set of finite binary words, and let Christoffel words be the usual Christoffel words over this alphabet. **$q$-analog of the Markoff injectivity conjecture.** The map

$$
w\longmapsto\mu_q(w)_{12}
$$

from $\\{\mathtt{0},\mathtt{1}\\}^*$ to $\mathbb{Z}[q]$ is injective over the set of Christoffel words. This is a $q$-analogue of the classical Markoff injectivity conjecture; the text notes that it is weaker than the classical conjecture because distinct polynomials can agree at $q=1$, and no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Sébastien Labbé and Mélodie Lapointe, “The q-analog of the Markoff injectivity conjecture over the language of a balanced sequence”, arXiv:2106.15886 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.15886

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2021).

record.title: Shen's conjecture on gradient conditions for magnetic Schrödinger operators
record.statement:
Let $n\geq 3$, let ${\bf B}$ be the magnetic field, and consider the magnetic Schrödinger operator $L_{{\bf a},V}$ with potential $V$. Theorem 0.11 of Shen concerns a bound on the number of negative eigenvalues when the potential has a non-trivial negative part.

**Shen's conjecture.** Some condition on $\nabla {\bf B}$ is necessary to prove Theorem 0.11 of Shen.

The source presents this as Shen's remark that a condition on the gradient of the magnetic field seems necessary, while the specific condition previously used is more restrictive than one would hope. The conjectural necessity of such a condition is not resolved here.
record.source_name: Bruno Poggi, “Applications of the landscape function for Schrödinger operators with singular potentials and irregular magnetic fields”, arXiv:2107.14103 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.14103

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2021).

record.title: The SP Goldbach conjecture for SP numbers
record.statement:
Let an **SP number** be a number of the form $pa^2$, where $p$ is prime and $a$ is a positive integer.

**SP Goldbach conjecture for SP numbers.** Every SP number greater than $27$ can be written as a sum of two SP numbers in at least one way.

This is a restricted form of the preceding additive conjecture: it concerns SP numbers as targets and is stated to begin at the explicit threshold $28$. The paper gives the example $153=28+125$, but no proof is supplied.
record.source_name: Raghavendra N. Bhat, “Distribution of Square Prime Numbers”, arXiv:2109.10238 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.10238

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2021).

record.title: The pure twin group right-angled Artin group conjecture
record.statement:
Let $T_n$ be the twin group, and let $PT_n$ be its pure subgroup, defined as the kernel of the natural surjection $T_n\to S_n$ given by $s_i\mapsto\tau_i$. A **right-angled Artin group** is a group admitting a presentation whose defining relations are commutators between selected pairs of generators.

**Pure twin group conjecture.** $PT_n$ is a right-angled Artin group for each $n\geq 3$.

The claim is known for $n=3,4,5$, while $PT_6$ is also known to be a right-angled Artin group through its description as a free product of $F_{71}$ and 20 copies of $\mathbb{Z}\oplus\mathbb{Z}$. The status for $n\geq 7$ remains open.
record.source_name: Tushar Kanta Naik, Neha Nanda and Mahender Singh, “Virtual planar braid groups and permutations”, arXiv:2109.13035 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.13035

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2021).

record.title: Compositional equivalences for pairs of length-four patterns
record.statement:
Let $C_n(\tau,\tau')$ be the set of all compositions of $n$ that avoid the patterns $\tau$ and $\tau'$, and let $c_n(\tau,\tau')=|C_n(\tau,\tau')|$. **Compositional equivalence conjecture.** If $n\geq 1$, then

$$
c_n(121,1342)=c_n(121,3142) \quad\text{and}\quad c_n(212,3124)=c_n(212,3142).
$$

These two equalities assert compositional equivalences that the authors' enumeration data suggest but that they are unable to prove by their present methods.
record.source_name: Vít Jelínek, Toufik Mansour, José L. Ramírez and Mark Shattuck, “Avoiding a pair of patterns in multisets and compositions”, arXiv:2111.06185 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.06185

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2021).

record.title: Balanced 3-partition conjecture for K_4-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $n$ be divisible by $3$ and let $G$ be a $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices. A balanced $3$-partition divides $V(G)$ into three classes of size $n/3$; class-edges are edges whose endpoints lie in the same class. **Balanced 3-partition conjecture for K_4-free graphs.** There exists a balanced $3$-partition with at most

$$
\frac{4}{81}n^2
$$

class-edges. This is one of the paper's open partition problems for $K_4$-free graphs, and no general resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: József Balogh, Felix Christian Clemen and Bernard Lidický, “10 Problems for Partitions of Triangle-free Graphs”, arXiv:2203.15764 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.15764

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2022).

record.title: The 106-color obstruction conjecture for partial 6-factorizations
record.statement: A **partial $6$-factorization** is a collection of edge-disjoint $6$-factors, called colors, in a sub-hypergraph of the complete $3$-uniform hypergraph $K_{10}^3$; an extension is a $6$-factorization of $K_{38}^3$ containing it. **The 106-color obstruction conjecture.** There exists a partial $6$-factorization of some sub-hypergraph of $K_{10}^3$ using 106 colors that cannot be extended to a $6$-factorization of $K_{38}^3$. This conjecture asserts that the number-of-colors bound achieved by the paper's construction is best possible; the supplied text gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Amin Bahmanian and Anna Johnsen, “Embedding Irregular Colorings into Connected Factorizations”, arXiv:2209.06402 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.06402

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2022).

record.title: Burstein's permutation enumeration conjecture for three pattern sets
record.statement:
Let $a(n)$ be defined by the unique formal power series solution

$$
\mathcal{A}(x)=\sum_{n\ge 1}a(n)x^n=x+2x^2+6x^3+23x^4+101x^5+480x^6+\cdots
$$

to

$$
\mathcal{A}(x)=\big(1+\mathcal{A}(x)\big)\big(x+\mathcal{A}(x)^2-x\mathcal{A}(x)^2\big).
$$

For a set of patterns $T$, let $\mathfrak{S}_n(T)$ denote the permutations of length $n$ avoiding every pattern in $T$. **Burstein's conjecture.** The value $a(n)$ counts the permutations of length $n$ that avoid one of the following sets of patterns:

$$
(3124,42153,24153),\quad (2134,42153,24153),\quad (2143,42135,24135).
$$

This is the first of Burstein's three conjectures concerning the sequence A218225; the paper proves the corresponding enumeration for the first pattern set, while the second and third conjectures remain open.
record.source_name: Shane Chern, Shishuo Fu and Zhicong Lin, “Burstein's permutation conjecture, Hong and Li's inversion sequence conjecture, and restricted Eulerian distributions”, arXiv:2209.12137 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.12137

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of September 2022); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Gao–Kitaev's enumerative conjecture for length-5 pattern-avoiding permutations
record.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{S}_n$ be the set of permutations of $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\mathfrak{S}_n(P_1,\ldots,P_r)$ denote the permutations avoiding the patterns $P_1,\ldots,P_r$. **Gao–Kitaev's conjecture.** For $n\geq 1$, the two avoidance classes have the same cardinality:

$$
|\mathfrak{S}_n(45312,45321,54312,54321)|=|\mathfrak{S}_n(31245,32145,31254,32154)|.
$$

The conjecture is an enumerative equality between two classes of permutations avoiding four patterns of length $5$. It is proved in this paper by constructing a bijection, so the conjecture is solved.
record.source_name: Joanna N. Chen and Zhicong Lin, “A bijection for length-5 patterns in permutations”, arXiv:2211.06871 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.06871

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of November 2022); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Monotonicity conjecture for the inconstructible-polyomino ratio
record.statement:
Let $P(n)$ be the number of polyominoes with $n$ cells. A polyomino is **constructible** if it is the concatenation of two polyominoes of smaller sizes, and **inconstructible** otherwise; let $Q(n)$ denote the number of inconstructible polyominoes with $n$ cells. **Inconstructible-polyomino ratio conjecture.** The sequence

$$
\frac{Q(n)}{P(n)}
$$

is decreasing. This conjecture is based on the available values of the sequences, computed up to $n=56$ in the source. Its resolution would provide the conjectural monotonicity needed for the paper's conditional upper-bound discussion, but no proof or disproof is given.
record.source_name: Vuong Bui, “An asymptotic lower bound on the number of polyominoes”, arXiv:2211.14909 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.14909

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2022).
